Sources indicate that the 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

According to recent reports, the ceremony took place on the evening of 17 November at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. It is the scene’s main end-of-season awards show. The event began in London in 2016.

At Worlds 2026, Caedrel was the top co-streamer for both hours watched and peak viewers, according to Esports Charts.

Industry observers note that his co-stream success came in a softer year for the tournament overall. Worlds 2026 peaked at 3.98 million viewers, which was 41% lower than the previous year. Caedrel’s numbers show how much attention a single co-streamer can hold even when the event’s headline peak falls.

Gaskin was not the only caster honoured in Miami. The other broadcast honours went to Alex ‘Machine’ Richardson for Play-by-Play Caster of the Year, Iain Chambers for Host of the Year and Anthony ‘NAMELESS’ Wheeler for Analyst of the Year. iShowSpeed was named Streamer of the Year.

Industry observers note that counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

In a recent development, vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

Don’t panic; it may look like you can’t recover the iconic livery, but you actually can: just visit the Vice Vinyl Mod shop in Vice City, and this garage should give you the option to restore the car's original livery/paint job.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the substantial Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

According to recent reports, patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

When you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Industry observers note that starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the newly introduced Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

If you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a new event that rewards you for killing enemies rapidly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

According to recent reports, elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a upcoming activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Recent findings suggest that anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

In a recent development, there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

In a recent development, even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the new season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the fresh class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

According to recent reports, season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

The more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

In a press release coinciding with Grand Theft Auto VI becoming available for pre-load ahead of its November 19th release date, Rockstar has confirmed that the game "has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits." Read between the lines, and you can kind of make out the words "...so hope your PCs are up to spec, computer nerds.".

GTA 6, of course, still does not have a confirmed PC version, even if Rockstar's former tech director claims it's probably not far off. And despite this, even ancient, last-gen consoles are getting in on it, as the release also unexpectedly confirms that the game will be playable on Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming, Microsoft's game streaming service that has suddenly lost its ability to work on PC. Granted, this comes with a warning: "as with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay." If you ended up getting a PS4 last generation, no cloud play for you either, I'm afraid. It also states that it will "play best on Playstation 5 consoles", making great use of that Sony partnership, and will include Playstation Spectral Super Resolution and ray-traced shadows on PS5 Pro.

A 2026 current-gen game targeting 30fps, let alone one as titanic of a release as GTA VI, is probably not going to go down well with a lot of people, even if console players are traditionally les sensitive about FPS counts than PC players. What this does imply, though, is that the inevitable PC release might be an even more demanding behemoth than expected, if Xbox Series and PS5 versions can't even target 60fps. The availability of the game on Xbox One, even if just through cloud streaming, could have resulted in an acceptance that 60fps just wasn't going to be possible if it was also going to be able to 'run' on last-gen hardware. Either way, when it does eventually escape console exclusivity, hopefully trying to run GTA VI on anything less than an RTX 5080 won't set your PC on fire. Now, let me just quickly have a glance at GPU prices. Oh, no.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA has successfully completed another powerful rocket engine test as the agency prepares for future Artemis missions that will return astronauts to the Moon and lay the groundwork for human exploration of Mars.

On November 18, engineers fired RS-25 engine No. 10001 at the Fred Haise Test Stand at NASA's Stennis Space Center, located near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. The developmental engine ran for its full scheduled duration of three minutes and 20 seconds (200 seconds).

It has been revealed that although this particular engine is not intended for spaceflight, the successful test will provide NASA and its primary contractor, L3Harris Technologies, with valuable performance data. Engineers will use the results to improve the power, efficiency, and reliability of RS-25 engines designed for upcoming Artemis missions.

Powerful RS-25 Engines Will Help Send Astronauts Back to the Moon.

According to recent reports, NASA is preparing for Artemis IV, a mission scheduled for 2028 that aims to land astronauts on the lunar surface. The mission will launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the massive Space Launch System (SLS) rocket to carry astronauts aboard the Orion spacecraft.

It has been revealed that artemis IV represents an important step toward NASA's larger ambitions. The agency aims to explore the Moon's South Pole, establish a sustained human presence on the lunar surface, and develop the experience and technologies needed for the first crewed journey to Mars.

The RS-25 engines play a crucial role in making these missions possible. Each SLS rocket uses four of the engines, which together generate up to 2 million pounds of thrust to help propel the spacecraft off the launchpad and into space.

Before any RS-25 engine is cleared for flight, it must undergo testing at NASA's Stennis Space Center to verify that it can perform reliably under the extreme conditions of a rocket launch.

These tests are carried out by specialists from NASA, L3Harris Technologies, and Nova Space Solutions, working together to ensure the engines are ready to power future journeys beyond Earth.

It has been revealed that to get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, which is the much easier way to get in. If you'd still rather unlock the safe the classic way, I'll explain both methods of getting into the safe below, including how to get the GTA 6 bowling alley safe code. Whichever road you go down, it'll help you save up some cash and get back on your feet - and take down a few of those pesky Kolt gang members while you're at it.

The GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300. To find it for yourself, you need to go to Brooks Boatworks, as hinted at in the notepad next to the safe. The safe code is on a map on the wall in one of the buildings there, as marked on the image above.

Sources indicate that by the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already. Whether you've been there or not, the map is found on the wall of an office in the raised buildings to the east of the area, and you can find two other GTA 6 safe codes on this map, too.

Sources indicate that you'll have to fend off a lot of Kolt members at both the bowling alley and the boatworks, so make sure you've got some decent GTA 6 guns to hand, and certainly as much Zombix as you can carry. You'll find more at each location, too, so keep an eye out.

In a recent development, you'll also see the option to plant explosives on the GTA 6 bowling alley safe, but if you haven't got the right explosives to hand, the option is grayed out. Fortunately, there are some sticky bombs conveniently stashed in the next room, meaning it's the much safer option that heading out to the boatworks.

We previously believed this option required reaching one of the Chapter 3 GTA 6 missions, at which point you unlock the ability to buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation, but with the few explosives available in the bowling alley, you're golden. Keep the spares on you, and you can use them to get into other safes around Leonida, too.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.
  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.
  • Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Enhancement to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside latest Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the major day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next significant game has officially released. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

Sources indicate that in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

It has been revealed that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

It has been revealed that indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#40618. Latest Update: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover

Latest Update: AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1346 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed.
  • For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works.
  • But the upcoming findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A fresh study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.

For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.

But the upcoming findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

Industry observers note that "Artificial intelligence systems are often described as 'brain-like' because they can predict activity in parts of the brain that help us recognize objects," notes York University Assistant Professor Kohitij Kar, senior author of a latest study. "Until now, scientists mostly tested this in one direction. They asked whether AI models can predict brain activity.".

A Latest Test Reveals a Hidden Problem With Brain-Like AI.

The York University team decided to approach this question from the opposite direction. Rather than simply measuring how well AI could predict the activity of brain cells, they investigated whether recorded brain activity could also predict what was happening inside the AI models.

If these systems truly operate like the brain, the researchers reasoned, the relationship should work in both directions. To investigate, they developed a method called reverse predictivity testing, which allowed them to evaluate similarities that conventional tests could overlook.

"Ultimately, we need computational models to truly understand the underlying neural mechanisms of how we recognize objects. How do we see objects move? While it's a very easy task that we do every day, computationally, though, it's a very challenging problem," notes Kar, the Canada Research Chair in Visual Neuroscience and a member of York's Centre for Vision Research and Centre for Integrative and Applied Neuroscience.

The research team, which included York Postdoctoral Fellow Sabine Muzellec, a trainee with the university's Connected Minds program, examined responses to a wide variety of visual images.

Industry observers note that their tests included 1,320 natural photographs and realistic synthetic images featuring 10 familiar subjects: a bear, an elephant, a face, an apple, a car, a dog, a chair, a plane, a bird, and a zebra. These objects appeared against a variety of natural scenes and indoor or outdoor backgrounds. The researchers also introduced 300 additional images showing the same subjects in different visual styles, including outlines, drawings, simplified representations, and artistic interpretations.

AI Can Predict Brain Activity, but the Reverse Tells a Different Story.

The results revealed a significant disconnect between artificial intelligence and biological vision.

Recent findings suggest that AI models were generally successful at predicting the responses of recorded neurons, which are the specialized cells that transmit information throughout the brain. However, when the researchers reversed the process, those same neuronal responses were much less effective at predicting many of the models' internal features.

This difference was particularly revealing because the researchers did not observe the same problem when comparing neuronal activity across different brains.

Sources indicate that "The results were striking. While AI models can predict the neurons we recorded in the brain fairly well, the brain cannot equally predict many of the model's internal features. Interestingly, this is not the case when neurons from one brain is compared against ones from another brain," indicates Kar.

Sources indicate that the findings suggest that an AI system can produce results that closely resemble those of the brain while relying on very different internal mechanisms. In other words, matching the brain's responses does not necessarily mean that the underlying processes are the same.

In a recent development, kar warns that this distinction could become increasingly notable as artificial intelligence advances. If researchers continue refining models based only on how accurately they predict neural activity, differences between those models and actual primate brains could accumulate over time.

That would undermine one of the main reasons neuroscientists use these systems in the first place: to develop realistic explanations of how the brain works.

"The findings suggest that today's AI systems solve visual tasks partly using internal strategies that the brain may not use. Importantly, the parts of AI models that align with the brain are also better at predicting real human behavior," states Kar.

Why the Discovery Matters for Neuroscience and Human Behavior.

The implications extend well beyond computer vision. Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to help researchers design experiments, study human behavior, and investigate neurological and psychological conditions. Many of these applications depend on the assumption that AI models process information in ways that resemble the human brain.

If that assumption is incorrect, researchers could draw misleading conclusions from models that appear accurate on the surface but operate differently underneath.

In a recent development, "Our findings challenge how similar current AI systems really are with the primate brain. We show that models that were previously thought to be brain-like rely on internal components that the brain does not appear to use. We provide a well-vetted diagnostic metric for the field," indicates Muzellec.

According to recent reports, developing AI systems that more faithfully reproduce brain function could eventually improve research into conditions ranging from post-traumatic stress disorder to autism. For now, however, the newly identified differences highlight the need for caution when using existing models to investigate human behavior or guide clinical research.

Industry observers note that the concern may also apply to other areas of neuroscience. Similar artificial intelligence models are already being used to study hearing, language, and movement. If those systems also rely on internal processes that differ from biological ones, researchers may need to reconsider how much they can reveal about the nervous system.

Building AI That More Closely Matches the Human Brain.

Rather than suggesting that artificial neural networks should be abandoned, the findings provide a way to make them more useful and scientifically reliable.

By identifying which features of an AI model correspond to real neural activity, researchers can focus on developing systems that more accurately reflect the biological mechanisms behind perception.

"Our approach helps identify which parts of an ANN truly match brain activity, allowing us to build more reliable models for understanding how people see and interpret the world," says Kar. "This is especially notable for our autism research program, which builds on models of the neurotypical brain as a baseline.".

Industry observers note that A neurotypical brain refers to one with patterns of neurological development and functioning generally considered typical. Establishing accurate models of these patterns is important for researchers investigating how perception and information processing may differ in conditions such as autism.

To help other scientists put their findings into practice, the team has released a publicly available testing toolkit that AI developers can use to evaluate their own models and identify opportunities for improvement.

It has been revealed that published in Nature Machine Intelligence, the study introduces a latest approach to evaluating artificial intelligence that goes beyond measuring how well a system performs a task. The researchers argue that understanding whether AI reaches its results through processes that genuinely resemble those of the brain is just as important.

The discovery could help guide the development of a fresh generation of AI models that not only recognize the world with impressive accuracy, but also offer a more faithful picture of how the human brain makes sense of what it sees.

According to recent reports, materials provided by York University. Original written by Sandra McLean. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

In a recent development, as another addition to the slew of smaller studios being dissolved by their parent companies, Bandai Namco revealed in a press release that they are shutting down their subsidiary studio Reflector Entertainment, a Montreal studio responsible for 2024's action-adventure game Unknown 9: Awakening. This is not the first time Reflector has been cut by Bandai, as around a month after the launch of Unknown 9: Awakening and presumably in response to its low sales, 18% of the workforce was laid off. 2025 then saw further redundancies amidst the cancellation of a prospective project, though details on those layoffs were not granted by the company. Unknown 9 was intended to be a transmedia franchise involving the game as well as comic books and novels, but these ambitions never came to pass.

Sources indicate that bandai Namco notes that the liquidation will be held to local laws and procedures, which make the actual schedule of the process uncertain for now. A similar process faces Arkane Lyon, which is at the moment in a purgatory of having been chosen for closure by Microsoft, but temporarily protected by French labor laws that prevent it from being suddenly closed without proper negotiation and procedure.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 has two main protagonists. They are Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and the pair are madly in love with one another. At least, you are going to want them to be. They have a chance to be more like friends by the end of the story.

They don’t automatically start off being thicker than thieves. Instead, they have a budding relationship that you must help develop, and there are multiple ways that you can help it grow and flourish throughout the game.

Recent findings suggest that you have to make sure to care about your partner, and not just treat them as any other character in the game. Do you think you can do that?

In a recent development, when you start up Grand Theft Auto 6, you play as Jason for a while. You don’t actually start playing as Lucia until the second chapter of the game. This is mostly because the first chapter is dedicated to her getting out of prison and adjusting to life outside.

When you get the call that she is getting out of prison soon, you need to start prepping the house if you want her to be happy. This means that you will want to fix the roof, outside steps, and the wall in the bedroom.

Each of these will help Lucia feel more at home and make her more happy when she gets out of prison, and it will give a serious boost to the relationship.

Your partner will drop hints in dialogue about things they expect you to do. For instance, Lucia and Jason will go to a bar shortly after she gets out of prison. During this time, she will ask Jason to grab her another drink.

If you don’t grab her a drink, it will be brought up in the next conversation, and it will ultimately decrease your relationship score because you didn’t listen to what she asked of you.

You need to pay attention to what your partner notes, and if they ask you to do something, it is important that you go out of your way to do it so they don’t get upset.

Early in the game, you need to set yourself up a BuckMe account. It is this game’s version of Venmo or PayPal, which allows you to send and receive money. It also lets you save money, and that is the key.

As part of the story, Lucia and Jason are saving up money for their family. This means that they need to put money aside for the future. This will also help them open a real bank account.

In a recent development, whenever you are able to, put money aside so that you can put it towards your future, as this will make your partner very happy. It reveals you are being responsible.

A substantial part of any relationship is showing your partner that you care and that you are there for them, and you can do this in multiple ways, but one way is physical affection. This can take many forms, even the simple holding of a hand.

Whenever Jason and Lucia are together, they have the option to hold hands. You will see the option to hold your partner’s hand in the bottom right corner of the screen. When this appears, it is good to pay attention to it.

Sources indicate that holding hands in public indicates your partner you are there with them and lets them know they can count on you. It’s a simple but vital gesture.

Another means of showing your partner that you care is purchasing them gifts. Everyone loves to get a gift, as it shows that they are being thought about, and the same applies for both Lucia and Jason in GTA 6.

There are various opportunities for you to purchase gifts for your partner. For instance, Jason can purchase a necklace for Lucia at the start of the game before she gets out of prison.

In a recent development, gifts don’t have to be lavish. Instead, you can simply think about what your partner is going to eat. Go out to the store and grab a couple of food items for them and they will definitely be happy about it.

It should go without saying that your partner should be the one you think of first when doing activities, but it might need to be spelled out for some people. Throughout the game, you have the opportunity to put the needs of your partner first or do other activities.

In a recent development, if you choose to do something else, they will be upset and you will lose points in your relationship. For instance, there is a time when Lucia will want Jason to talk to Mattia.

Sources indicate that if you choose to do other things first, like hang out with Cal, Lucia will be noticeably upset with Jason that he chose to do something else before the thing she asked him to do. Putting your partner first will increase your relationship score quickly.

Industry observers note that after a while, you will have full access to Vice City and the glorious sun-baked land of Leonida. That means that you have plenty of activities you can take part in. At this point in the game, you will be playing the game mostly as a duo, which means you can take part in activities together.

According to recent reports, there are games that can be played like mini-golf, and then there’s other stuff like kayaking that you can do. These are all considered dates, and they are vital to take part in, as they will immensely help your relationship.

As part of the dating mechanic, your partner will mention things they are interested in doing, and taking part in these activities will increase your bond, so make sure you pay attention to what they say while you are out and about.

It has been revealed that A big part of GTA 6 is the ability to play as both Jason and Lucia. Rockstar made a big deal about being able to seamlessly switch between these two as you complete missions and explore the world.

This means that you can take on heists by yourself or you can complete the job with your partner, and it is better overall to do the latter.

According to recent reports, having your partner with you means that you have twice the manpower, and it also means that you can get more loot, and someone watching your back for if trouble comes. Plus, it raises your relationship status to have your partner in crime by your side.

Nintendo reinstates SmileBasic 4 to the eShop after it was used for Switch 2 jailbreaks

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (449 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop.
  • SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing users to code their own simple programs and games.
  • Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SmileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop. While the console's firmware has long since been updated to stop known jailbreak exploits, SmileBasic 4 itself has now also been patched.

SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing users to code their own simple programs and games. It's also opened multiple backdoors for jailbreak exploits over the years, first on 3DS, and then on Switch 2.

Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo. That would allow owners to, in theory, run homebrew applications, but as far as I can tell, the exploit had not yet been extended to allow people to play pirated games.

Industry observers note that nonetheless, Nintendo acted quickly to delist SmileBasic 4 from the eShop and to update the console's firmware to address the exploit at a system level. That's a necessary step, too, as SmileBasic 4 was not the only application that could be used to exploit it. Notably, Civilization 7, a game that is available on cartridge and thus impervious to delistings and software updates, could also be used for the jailbreak.

Even so, it seems that SmileBasic 4 itself has been updated to ensure that a similar exploit never happens again. As Twitter user MarioMasta64 notes, the software itself has gotten a fresh update post-reinstatement aimed at closing the hole used for the jailbreak. The application's demo – which could also be used to exploit it – has also been updated, but it has not yet been relisted on the eShop.

  • It has been revealed that team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3.
  • According to recent reports, today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • It has been revealed that to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related concerns.

According to recent reports, today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

It has been revealed that to begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja remarked it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

It has been revealed that the amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

It has been revealed that in the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

It has been revealed that you can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

In a recent development, there’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

Company of Heroes 3 developer admits "it was a lot" to make the 3.0 overhaul patch alongside regular updates, singleplayer DLC, and a whole spinoff game

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1047 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Firm of Heroes 3's 3.0 patch is huge.
  • Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.
  • The team began planning the 3.0 patch two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Company of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Firm of Heroes 3's 3.0 patch is huge. Touching virtually every part of the three-year-old RTS, the patch notes are longer than, well, my arm isn't a great measure of patch note length. Let's just say the headline features of overhauled VFX and audio don't really cover it. It also comes with new autumn and winter biomes, an updated grand strategy campaign, improvements to unit AI, and a whole host of other changes.

Talking to Relic ahead of the 3.0 update's launch I learned a little more about the scale of work that went on behind the scenes to make it happen, but also a little more about why Relic are still supporting the game three years after it was released and two years after separating from Sega.

The team began planning the 3.0 patch two years ago, seeing the series' 20th anniversary as an opportunity to make a significant update to Company of Heroes 3, and focus on issues players had flagged since launch. "The VFX were called out," executive producer Denise Christie tells me. "Same thing with a lot of our audio.".

In a recent development, relic were already releasing patches every three months, but the changes they were looking at were much too large for those smaller updates. If they had tried to do the work as part of the small updates, approaching the problems with piecemeal solutions, it would have turned Firm of Heroes 3 into a hodgepodge of new and old assets. "We wanted to make sure it was a cohesive package," principal designer Eric Wrobel indicates. "If you increase the quality of one thing, you have to do it equally across so much stuff." Otherwise you end up with "One that looks awesome and one that's like, 'Oh, this one's kind of gross'.".

Complicating matters, though, was that the team couldn't down tools and focus on just these large changes. As well as the small patches that were still going out every three months, both the VFX and audio teams were also contributing the battlegroup DLC packs which added newly introduced units to the game. "They would work on stuff and in one branch that was the 3.0 work and then they would go ahead and do some battlegroup stuff and come back to that," Christie says. "It was a lot.".

Sources indicate that as the 3.0 update grew in scope, it also meant other departments were contributing to the anniversary release while working on the smaller updates and DLC. "For us to create future maps for Company of Heroes 3, we were going to have an issue that our assets were getting stale," Christie explains. So, as part of 3.0, Relic's art department created autumn and winter asset packs, as well as a upcoming Industrial theme. This then created more work for the VFX team, who have added rain and snow, as well as a transition effect showing soil and concrete moving from dry to wet.

Not to be outdone, the design team also made significant changes to the singleplayer Italy campaign. The towns that dot the dynamic grand strategy-inspired map now have individual upgrades, making for more meaningful decisions when it comes to which settlement you capture next. And, responding to one of the main criticisms of Tech giant of Heroes 3's singleplayer, they also updated the computer's AI so it makes smarter decisions in both the turn-based and real-time battles. "We wanted to get this feel like there was that sort of back and forth of the AI resisting you and pushing forward into your territory and actually taking your stuff, which wasn't really happening in any of the previous updates," Wrobel indicates.

In a recent development, further complicating matters was the fact that alongside these regular updates, the DLC, and the substantial 3.0 update release work, was that Relic also released Final Stand in July, a roguelike horde mode spinoff of Company of Heroes 3. "We had to be very careful not to accidentally introduce this 3.0 work that was also happening at the same time," Christie says." The improvements in this update have also rolled out for the spinoff, too.

According to recent reports, naturally, Relic aren't doing all this work purely out of the goodness of the hearts. The regular updates keep players engaged, Christie explains, and "hopefully bring back lapsed players who were frustrated by some of these things." It's something the team have already seen happen before, Wrobel explains. "We saw with the 2.0 revision that we had a big spike of consumers and that was great, but because that improved the overall quality of the game, we saw each month we were selling more copies than we were before. People have been buying these games for years and years and years, so if we invest in this now we're going to see returns for quite a long time into the future as well.".

"If we were starting to see that tail down then we probably would have made a very different decision to be honest, but that's not what we see," Christie adds.

According to recent reports, the next release for Manufacturer of Heroes 3 is a singleplayer DLC, Operation Torch, due out on November 25th. (So, if you're keeping count, that was also in the works while the update, battlegroup DLC, and spinoff were all being made.) Until now, Relic's additions to the RTS have been focused on the multiplayer community, adding fresh units to be used online or in offline skirmishes. Operation Torch brings new scripted missions that trace a set of soldiers moving through North Africa.

After that, though, I ask if Relic plans to continue adding to Company of Heroes 3 or if they're ready to move onto a newly introduced project. "Well, it's both actually," CEO Justin Dowdeswell tells me. "We would love to continue with Company of Heroes 3 and not solely as a place for us to experiment. That's one of the advantages of being smaller, and being able to make decisions. We're not going to leave Company of Heroes 3. It's an and function. We are going to embark on the next thing.".

So, it doesn't sound like Relic are taking anything off their plate….

The Sims 4 will soon get a new patch to resolve a number of problems, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it looks to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

In a recent development, you can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

In a recent development, going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Industry observers note that speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis stated this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

It has been revealed that pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in newly introduced saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a upcoming lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

It has been revealed that lower down the list of urgent fixes is an revision that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently unveiled that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override releases in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

In a recent development, shopify Rebellion Black opened the North America Qualifier Playoffs with a 2-0 win over Xora Esports. The non-partner organisation is now one win from the playoffs that decide a guaranteed São Paulo Kickoff place.

The best-of-three Group Stage meeting with Xora began at 00:10, opening Shopify Rebellion Black’s VCT Americas Kickoff: North America 2027 campaign.

The result counts for more because Shopify Rebellion is now outside Riot’s partnership system. The organisation was one of the Americas sides that noted it had not been chosen for the 2027-2028 partnership programme, Sheep Esports reported. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

Shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

According to recent reports, across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

The organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

Recent findings suggest that the prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

  • However, finding a plane is easier said than done.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that planes are, without a doubt, the fastest way to get around the map in GTA VI. They can help you explore areas to find points of interest or simply get to a pinged location in a flash.

However, finding a plane is easier said than done. In GTA VI, planes are typically found in very specific locations such as airports and airstrips.

If you are looking for a sweet plane to take up into the skies, you have come to the right place. Here are the best places to get a plane in Grand Theft Auto VI.

Sources indicate that players can find an airstrip on the southeast side of the Grassrivers in Mariana County. This airstrip has a plane that’s easy to control, and there is usually no one around, making it easy to steal.

In the northern section of Belville in Leonard County, you will find Lake Leonida. Next to one of the docks on the lake, you will find a plane that’s easy to steal because the open water acts as a runway and there aren’t many people around.

In a recent development, in Borrachero Sound, a very small area on the west side of Kelly County, you will find an airstrip that lies next to the water. You'll usually find more than one plane here, so you’ll have options to choose from.

In the Waning Sands region of Leonard County, you will find an airstrip just outside of Belville. Similar to the plane spot mentioned earlier, you will also find more than one plane at this airstrip.

Industry observers note that last, but certainly not least, one of the best places to find a plane is, of course, the Vice City International Airport. Known as VCIA, you can find this airport in the southwest section of Vice Dale County.

Keep in mind that VCIA has high security, so stealing a plane can be tricky. However, it is an airport, so it has the most planes available, making it one of the best places to find one.

If you’d like to get a plane in a more natural way, that doesn’t involve stealing, you can find one during the McKittrick Farm side quest. To start this quest, examine the poster inside the Starlet Motel office (mandatory location in Chapter 2), and the location of the farm will be marked on your map.

Recent findings suggest that since you’ll be stealing the planes mentioned in this guide, it’s wise to learn how to avoid the cops when flying. Even though the places I mentioned here tend to have almost no one around, with the exception of VCIA, there’s still a possibility that someone will spot you stealing it or report the crime once they realize it's missing.

According to recent reports, the best way to avoid cops' detection when flying a plane is to fly at low altitude. Flying low makes it harder for cops to see you, as buildings, trees, and other structures will help block their line of sight.

Industry observers note that you only really need to worry about this if the heat star level reaches 3 to 4, when police bring in the helicopters. Otherwise, you can easily lose cops by simply flying away due to how fast planes go in the game.

If I wasn't so sick of hearing about AI every day of my life at the moment I might have found it funny to hear that one of the biggest peddlers of the poison around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was caught having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Oh who am I kidding, it is funny! And despite knowing that this won't likely push Nvidia away from AI, I am a bit tickled to hear that the tech company and Huang are on the receiving end of a lawsuit.

The suit in question, as reported by The Guardian, is based on a complaint filed in California's federal court on behalf of Mark Kistenmacher by Rosen Law Firm. Kistenmacher is an Nvidia shareholder, and with this suit he's seeking to "recover compensable damages," for himself and other shareholders due to the "precipitous decline in the market value of the Tech giant’s securities." What a palaver! I do not imagine this will be resolved particularly promptly.

Recent findings suggest that as it currently stands, Huang has only admitted to having an affair rather than any trade secrets being leaked anywhere. Nvidia had this to say on the matter: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it. The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.".

The concern comes from the person Huang had an affair with, one Alice Huang (no, they aren't related), a former managing director of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company who have allegedly given Chinese companies Nvidia chips they bought billions of US dollars of. A messy situation to be sure, and one I unconfidently hope brings about the end of AI, somehow.

In a recent development, crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

Sources indicate that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

Recent findings suggest that with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It has been revealed that it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

Industry observers note that since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Industry observers note that alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

I was honestly flabbergasted.".

The discontent continued throughout the thread, with many pointing to Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas' CJ as an example of the heft they'd have liked to see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

According to recent reports, the standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the organization's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be confirmed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

Industry observers note that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Industry observers note that last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has declared that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Industry observers note that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has declared that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Industry observers note that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

According to recent reports, once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the latest Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

According to recent reports, casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for latest players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Recent findings suggest that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

Sources indicate that the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

It has been revealed that this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big fresh update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

Latest Update: 10 Game Boy Metroidvanias You Can Finish in Under 10 Hours

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games.
  • Very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania.
  • Industry observers note that the Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For a long time, Metroidvanias have been a bit of an oddball when compared to some other games. They’re still great games, sometimes the best titles of a console generation, but back in the day they were more niche.

Very few games ever even attempted to push the envelope of Metroidvanias aside from those that coined the term, Metroid and Castlevania. One of the biggest draws of these games is that you could complete them pretty quickly, especially when it came to the handheld consoles.

Industry observers note that the Game Boy, Game Boy Color, and Game Boy Advance could see players complete the game in one long car ride, provided it wasn’t too dark outside just yet. This list encompasses the shortest Metroidvanias of the broader Game Boy generation that you could finish in under ten hours.

Starting off with a strange one that fits a bit more into a Metroidvania-like category, Wario Land 3 did incorporate a lot of aspects of Metroidvanias. Playing as the treasure-obsessed Wario, players would navigate various levels attempting to find all the treasure chests available.

It has been revealed that in true Metroidvania fashion, players could return to older levels of the game with fresh abilities to uncover other secrets they couldn’t get to before. The game did manage to make a name for itself thanks to some innovative gameplay elements and its relatively quick run-through.

According to recent reports, now the Castlevania series is absolutely a true Metroidvania, and one of the more difficult by many people's standards. Playing as Nathan Graves, players will enter Dracula’s Castle in an attempt to rescue their mentor.

According to recent reports, while not part of the main continuity of Castlevania, the game gained a following thanks to the difficulty and use of the Dual Set-Up System. This system gave players the ability to create new combinations of attacks via a card-collecting system, for interesting results.

Many of the best Castlevania games incorporate some sort of gimmick to make them a bit more interesting, and Castlevania: Harmony of Dissonance is no exception. Fifty years before Simon Belmont took on Dracula, there was Juste Belmont and their journey through Dracula’s Castle.

The main feature of the game was the two versions of Dracula’s Castle that saw players moving between the two to solve mysteries and unlock paths intertwined between them. That’s probably the reason the game is on the longer side compared to most of the other Metroidvanias of the time.

In a surprising twist, this Castlevania game is actually set in the future, in 2035. It also abandoned the Belmonts for a brand newly introduced protagonist, Soma Cruz, who would discover his strange ability after being drawn to the castle during an eclipse.

In keeping with the lore of the game, the major system here was called the Tactical Soul System, and it would allow Soma to gain newly introduced abilities based on the soul he collected. This drove the main idea behind the Metroidvania aspects of the game and granted some freedom in character builds that players enjoyed.

It has been revealed that whether you’ve heard of the series or seen something from it, almost everyone can recognize Shantae for one reason or another. The series launched in 2002 with some great Metroidvania elements that gained a large following, making it fairly popular.

Industry observers note that the game introduced players to the half-genie protagonist Shantae as she did battle against her arch-nemesis Risky Boots. The key feature of the game was that Shantae could dance to transform herself into animals to perform different tasks and movement challenges, accessing other areas.

Industry observers note that the first Metroid game on the list, but not the first to pioneer the series, Metroid Fusion was the fourth game in the series. It brought a different kind of focus to the series, with the game sticking more to narrative and suspense than previous installments.

Sources indicate that this proved to be a great idea as the game revolved around Samus Aran and the infamous SA-X, a duplicate made with an infected suit. It brought an air of suspense to the game that stuck with players despite how short the game was.

Recent findings suggest that unlike some of the other Metroid games, Metroid: Zero Mission sought to enhancement the original game for a more modern era. Zero Mission introduced a lot of quality-of-life features to make the age of the original game a bit more manageable.

It has been revealed that the game took pieces from previous titles that it had learned from, incorporating more story and expanded content. While still short, Metroid: Zero Mission managed to set a latest path for the Metroid series as a whole, and is still seen as one of its highlights.

According to recent reports, the second game in the series, Metroid II: Return of Samus, is one of the most iconic of all. This title introduced a few of the most memorable features that would become staples of the series, like the Spider Ball.

Recent findings suggest that not only did the game introduce some new mechanics, but it also focused on a darker world and story for the Metroidvania. The game clearly helped to build a dedicated fanbase despite its shortness, as its influences can be seen even in the newer Metroid releases today.

Sources indicate that A Metroidvania before the genre was even established, TMNT III: Radical Rescue was arguably one of the first few Metroidvanias. It featured a story focused on rescuing the turtles from the claws of Shredder in a beat-em-up exploration-focused game.

Each of the four turtles had a special use that would unlock more of the map for you to explore, effectively making the game a great Metroidvania-style game. There’s certainly an argument to be made that it would go on to inspire features in the genre.

Industry observers note that A controversial title that ended up being basically expelled from the series for narrative reasons. It was a bit different from other entries in the series, being a more stage-based game rather than focusing on traditional navigation.

In a recent development, regardless of any of that, the game is the shortest Metroidvania from the Game Boy era, clocking in at around two hours total. While perhaps not the most important Metroidvania over the years, it certainly has its place in history and our hearts. What a little curio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, marathon is getting a lot bigger next month. In September, Bungie outlined their looks for the shooter making some big promises, namely the arrival of a PvE mode, and now they've shown off what you can expect from its next season, Symbiosis.

Industry observers note that top of the order is that PvE mode, which has a name now: Expedition. It's a roguelite mode, one that's playable in co-op, though a lack of details at this current time doesn't make it clear as to whether you can run it solo or not. The season's trailer, which you can have a gander at below, gives off the impression that you'll have to complete particular tasks before exfiltrating like you normally do. I'm sure we'll learn more in time.

Industry observers note that the previously promised social space will be coming with this patch too, and it's called Limbo. Morbidly appropriate! You can hang out here with your buds, head to a mini arena for some impromptu matches (I think), or head to the firing range where you can test out your weapons. You'll also be able to try out the fresh runner shell, Bishop, a cooler than you, samurai-sword-wielding robot who can jump real good and do that cool movie thing where it slices a whole bunch of enemies at once in one swing real quick like.

What will undoubtedly have some folks going "Halo's back!" is the beginning of a beta test for a team deathmatch mode. The Halo comparison is apt not simply because of the fact that it's Bungie who are making it, but because there's a deep-voiced announcer guy talking about all the sick kills you do. Details are slim on how this will work too. Beyond that, there's a few new weapons to flaunt, and maybe most excitingly, massive ole alien enemies to take on.

You've still got a little while to wait for Symbiosis, which is presently slated to launch on December 8th. The game will be free to play from then until December 15th, too, obviously in a bid to show sceptics how good it is now (hopefully it is good, for Bungie's sake).

💡 Key Takeaways
